name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+19 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely
Daniel Biss has raised nearly $3 million with outside groups active on both sides, while John Elleson shows no reported fundraising
Open seat after Jan Schakowsky's retirement removes incumbency but not the district's structural advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+19 lean, Biss's large financial advantage, and markets pricing the Democratic side near 97% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals with slightly reduced margin for open-seat uncertainty.
model.watch: Any sign of Republican fundraising or outside spending surging into this Chicago-area seat, or a divisive Democratic primary aftermath, would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat open, but the district's D+19 partisan lean gives Democrats a strong structural advantage. Daniel Biss, a well-known former state legislator and gubernatorial primary contender, has raised nearly $3 million and drawn outside spending from both supporting and opposing groups. Republican John Elleson shows no reported fundraising in the available data.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democratic side near 97%. An open seat adds some uncertainty, but the district's composition makes a Republican upset highly unlikely.
